dek: Miami's hookah scene ranked: 10 lounges from Little Haiti to a Wynwood rooftop.

slides.label: NYC Energy
slides.text: Miami has always felt like a *small New York* to me, so I ranked its hookah spots bowl first, bottle last.

slides.label: Why Now
slides.text: Miami built its name on the *bottle parade*. The slow money's on the bowl now, and nobody rushes a bowl.

slides.label: The Rules
slides.text: I rank on the *hookah only*: smoke, flavors, coals, price. Food, bottles and DJs just break ties.

slides.label: #1 Pick
slides.text: No.1: *Mood Miami Hookah* in Little Haiti. About $20 buys the hookah, coals ride free. Cash only, open til 3AM.

slides.label: Rooftop Steal
slides.text: No.7: the rooftop at *La Ferneteria* in Wynwood, nine floors up, hookahs start at just $15.

slides.label: Price Range
slides.text: Across Miami, hookah runs *$15 to $80*: cheapest on the Wynwood rooftop, priciest in Brickell and Miami Beach.

slides.label: Fine Print
slides.text: Hookah isn't a wellness swap: the CDC says it carries *many of the same risks* as cigarettes. Pace yourself.

slides.label: Last Puff
slides.text: Miami always knew how to go out. Now it's learning how to *stay put*: one bowl, one table, no clock.

caption_linkedin:
Miami's hookah lounges are a small case study in how a city's nightlife economy shifts when the margin moves.

For years the bottle was the business model: sparklers, countdowns, a bill with its own security detail. Now the slow, steady money is on the bowl. One directory puts a standard hookah at $25 to $40 in Doral and $50 to $80 in Brickell and Miami Beach, and several of the best rated rooms on our list come in well under that.

That's a useful lesson for anyone building a hospitality business right now: the headline item doesn't have to be the most expensive one. Mood Miami Hookah charges about $20 and still packs the room. The rooftop at La Ferneteria undercuts the market at $15 and sits nine floors over Wynwood.

We ranked the city's top 10 lounges the way we'd judge any product: the thing itself first, the add ons second.

What's winning in your market right now, the bottle or the bowl?
